Resource usage
Export Stack

JSON follows the original HyperCardPreview model. Pictures are exported separately, as in the Mac application.

Gallery / preview cardsthrough


Both views are included in every gallery. Storyboard shows 60 cards per page; select a thumbnail to inspect the card.

Includes JSON, card/background pictures, card previews, original resource bytes, supported PNG/WAV/text conversions, a static analysis report, and an export report. JSON and original artwork cover the entire stack; rendered previews use the selected range. Large stacks start with previews off.

Card previews use matching imported bitmap fonts where supported and browser fallback otherwise. Original bitmap layers and raw resource bytes are preserved separately. The original input is never changed.
Field Data · by background

CSV export

Export the selected background. Shared background fields repeat their shared value; other background fields use each card’s own text. Missing values remain empty. Card fields form separate columns by field ID.

Literal text adds an apostrophe before values starting with =, +, − (ASCII -), or @, including after whitespace. Turn it off for exact original text. CSV always quotes values and doubles quotation marks. Original line breaks are retained unless normalization is selected. Export is cancellable and limited to 64 MiB; narrow the range for larger data.

Static Stack & Dependency Map

● Stored structure/resources ● Literal target ┄ Inferred candidate ┄ Unresolved expression

What this map shows: a diagram of what is in the stack and what its scripts appear to reference. Each node is an item, such as a card, background, button, field or resource. An arrow points from the item containing or making a reference to the item it refers to; it does not mean that the program has run.

How to read this map
  1. Choose an item from the list on the left. The selected item appears in the center; incoming references appear to its left and outgoing references to its right.
  2. Follow a neighboring node to explore it, or use Inspect selected to see its properties or script. For example, a button may point to a card named in its script, or to its icon resource.
  3. Use the filters to separate stored structure and literal references from inferred candidates. Dashed links need interpretation: computed targets may remain unresolved and a candidate handler may never be called.

Select a node to explore incoming and outgoing relationships. Arrows show reference direction. Static inspection does not execute scripts or resolve message dispatch. Inferred calls may have multiple candidates; computed, relative, missing or external targets remain unresolved.

Stack

60 nodes and 24 relationships per page. Index limits: 50,000 nodes, 100,000 edges, 20 handler candidates per call; resource-link omissions are reported. No traced references does not mean a resource is unused. SVG exports the current focus/page; JSON exports the retained index, including omissions.
Bookmarks & Review Notes

Keep bookmarks and plain-text notes about cards, controls, backgrounds, the stack or resources. Reviews are separate from the original stack. Export review JSON to keep your work after closing this application. Open the same stack with the same artwork/resources, then import or drop the review JSON onto this window to resume. No scripts run.

Portable review files and limits

Stack identity checks include stored data, scripts, artwork and resource bytes; filenames and display caches are ignored. Another export format or missing resource fork/artwork may have a different identity even if the cards look similar. Review import requires a matching identity. Targets use stored IDs; missing or duplicate IDs are never guessed. Imported JSON is data and is never executed.

Import merges entries and keeps the local copy when an entry ID already exists. Export also records your current viewer location when this review matches the stack; Resume saved location returns there. Reviews remain in memory across stack switches, with no automatic disk or browser storage. Limits: 60 entries per page, 5,000 entries / 8 MiB per file, 16,384 characters per note, eight open reviews / 32 MiB total. Identity checking is cancellable and capped at 256 MiB of loaded content.

Author: Michael Roberts · Creation / Revision: October 10, 2026.
Contains AI-generated content.

A desktop, offline preview and export tool inspired by Pierre Lorenzi’s HyperCardPreview.

Open files

Open original HyperCard 1.x/2.x data forks, MacBinary, AppleSingle, BinHex/HQX, exported JSON, or standard ZIP archives and supported classic StuffIt .sit archives. Select a matching .rsrc or AppleDouble (._name) file with its stack. A browser cannot automatically read a Mac file’s hidden resource fork: retain it in a ZIP with AppleDouble metadata or select a separately saved fork.

HQX & StuffIt archives

Open or drop BinHex 4.0 (.hqx) and supported classic StuffIt (.sit) files directly. Both formats can retain the original data and resource forks. HQX is an encoding wrapper and can contain a stack or another archive; supported HQX-wrapped StuffIt and MacBinary archives are opened automatically. Preserved resources supply saved color, pictures, icons and fonts.

StuffIt support covers the classic SIT! / STi archive layout (catalog version 0–1) with Stored, RLE, LZW and Huffman methods (0–3). StuffIt 5, StuffIt X, linked catalogs, encrypted/segmented archives and other methods need external extraction. Unsupported or damaged archives fail with an explanation; their resources are not silently omitted. For these files, extract with a Macintosh-aware utility, then use Finder Compress on the extracted original stack and companions to make a resource-preserving ZIP. Encoding or compressing a file after its resource fork was lost cannot restore it.

Browse & inspect

Arrow keys or Page Up/Down change cards. Home/End jump to first/last. Enter switches the card grid. Command/Ctrl+O opens files. Inspect Objects makes objects clickable; right-click the card to list overlapping objects. The Objects tab also lists hidden controls. Select field text to copy it, or copy text and scripts from the inspector. Search includes object names, text and scripts, including stack/background scripts.

Health & search

Health reviews the loaded stack after import and reports structural issues, missing icons and display limitations. Findings link to cards, objects or resources; download the report or find STACK_HEALTH.json in the complete ZIP. Absence of a resource fork alone does not establish data loss. Search options offers field text, scripts, names and resources, Match case and Whole word. Results show the first match per card plus matching resources, with highlighted excerpts and direct inspection links.

Open or drop a ZIP — recommended for classic Mac stacks

You can drag a ZIP containing a HyperCard stack onto this application or select it with Open files. The application reads the archive directly; you do not need to extract it first. On your Mac, use Finder’s Compress command on the original stack or a folder containing the stack and its companion pictures.

Classic Mac stacks have a data fork for cards/text/scripts and may have a separate resource fork for saved AddColor definitions, color PICT pictures, icons, fonts and external commands. Uploading or copying the bare file can lose that resource fork. A resource-preserving Mac ZIP carries it alongside the stack, allowing the application to load both. Compressing a copy that has already lost its resources cannot restore them. Color Tools was verified with its original Mac ZIP.

Field data & CSV

Field Data groups cards by background, including shared and per-card text and card-owned fields. Browse 60 cards and 12 fields per page, click a value to read/copy its complete text or inspect its field, and select columns for CSV. Exports include all selected columns across field pages and the chosen card range within the background. Delimiter, headings, UTF-8 signature, line-break normalization and formula-like literal text are configurable.

Resource workbench

Resources offers List and Thumbnails views, type/name/ID filters, sorting and 60-item pages. Select individual resources, the current page or all matches; selections remain selected across filters and pages. Extract selected ZIP offers original payloads, originals plus supported previews, or previews with original fallback when conversion is unsupported. Export all resources includes the full collection. Reopen an extracted resource ZIP while a stack is loaded to add missing resources; existing type/ID entries are kept.

Find uses traces supported icon IDs, field fonts and saved color/picture declarations. Select a location to inspect its card or background. No traced references does not mean a resource is unused: scripts and other stacks can still reference it.

Fonts & rendering

Health → Fonts & rendering inventories requested fonts, sizes, styles and browser fallback choices, with measured browser-font metrics. Download the audit, or find FONT_AUDIT.json in a complete ZIP. Styled field text now retains run fonts, sizes, underline, outline/shadow and condensed/extended spacing in PNG and gallery previews. Imported monochrome FONT/NFNT glyphs and FOND associations now support matching strikes. Appearance can switch to browser fonts. Unsupported sizes/styles/glyphs fall back. Live fields with bitmap strikes use measured canvas text with a selectable text layer. Saved AddColor overlays can be toggled on/off; Health → Color report lists omissions.

AddColor & pictures

Color on/off shows or hides saved AddColor declarations. It does not run color scripts or external commands. Saved overlays preserve black ink; the same choice applies to PNG, thumbnails and gallery exports. Color resources can show supported TIFF/PICT pictures; unsupported pictures remain raw. Health → Color report lists omissions and missing references.

Large stacks

The card list and gallery display 30, 60 or 120 cards per page. Search scans the entire stack, and direct card jumps reveal the correct page. Analysis, resource and object lists are also paged. Stack parsing, analysis and ZIP assembly use background workers when available. Cancel operation stops a pending search, background operation or export.

Choose a gallery / preview range in Export. Complete ZIP exports retain all JSON and original artwork; rendered previews follow that range. Stacks above 500 cards default to previews off. Gallery output is limited to 64 MiB; ZIP output to 128 MiB. Use a smaller range or omit previews for large exports.

Appearance & welcome

Welcome returns to the opening screen without unloading the stack; Resume stack restores your view. Appearance offers Pearl or Classic glass surfaces, eight accent colors, reduced transparency and increased contrast. Imported card artwork and field geometry retain their original styling. System reduced motion and supported accessibility preferences are respected.

Bookmarks & review notes

Review adds portable bookmarks, plain-text notes, tags and review statuses. Choose a current card, selected viewer object, stack or selected resource; add an entry and Save. Search/filter the paged list and Inspect target to return to it. Export review JSON saves the session and current location. To resume, open the same stack (including artwork/resource companions), Import & merge review, then Resume saved location. Imported sessions must match the loaded-content fingerprint; different revisions or formats may not match. Local entries win merge conflicts. Saved entries survive stack switches in this open application, but are not automatically stored on disk. Export before closing; the original stack is unchanged.

Stack & dependency map

The map is a static diagram of the stack’s contents and references. Nodes represent items; arrows point from the container or referring item to the referenced item. Select a node on the left to see incoming references on the left of the diagram and outgoing references on the right. A button can point to a named destination card or its icon. The map does not run the program or prove that an inferred handler is called.

Map explores cards, shared backgrounds, fields/buttons, literal navigation, sent-message target candidates, inferred handler/external candidates and supported resource references. Filter nodes and relationship evidence, select a neighbor to refocus, and inspect sources. Computed/relative/external targets stay unresolved. Export the focused page as SVG or the retained relationship index as JSON. Limits and omissions are explicit.

Analyze

Analyze inventories all scripts and handlers, globals, navigation, sent messages and XCMD/XFCN resources. Select an entry to inspect its script, or download the analysis JSON. Literal card targets can be opened directly. Computed targets, message routing and external behavior are not evaluated. The scanner is not a full HyperTalk syntax validator.

Compatibility

This application preserves data rather than promising pixel-perfect display. Matching imported monochrome bitmap fonts and saved AddColor overlays can be previewed. Color on/off applies to the viewer, thumbnails and PNG previews; exported galleries include both variants. Health → Color report explains omitted saved declarations. TIFF and PICT decoding supports bounded subsets, with approximate bevels and control curves. Script-created color, unsupported sound codecs, encrypted private-access stacks and unsupported StuffIt variants are deferred. Unsupported pictures and resources remain available as exact raw bytes.

Desktop target: modern Chrome, Firefox and Safari. ZIP import requires raw-DEFLATE support; if unavailable, extract the archive and select the files together. Automated browser validation is reported in the accompanying README.

Resource export formats

Export supported graphics as full-size PNG and sounds as playable PCM WAV. Select a resource to see its format, dimensions or audio details and conversion status. PNG includes supported PICT/TIFF pictures, monochrome icons/cursors, color icons and bitmap font specimen strips. WAV supports standard and extended 8/16-bit mono/stereo PCM and MACE 3:1/6:1 sounds. Select Original + modern formats to retain original payloads alongside conversions; unsupported resources always retain their originals. Export all resources ZIP and Complete export ZIP use the same conversions. Sound is exported once at its native sample rate; loops and commands are not executed. Conversion details and sound metadata are recorded in RESOURCE_CONVERSIONS.json. Color icons use embedded or matching companion masks; missing masks export opaque. Bitmap font strips are images, not installable fonts.

Stack Analysis
Appearance
System accessibility preferences are also respected. Imported card artwork retains its original appearance.
Stack Health


Search & Results
First match per card, followed by matching resources. Shared scripts can match multiple cards. Resource search includes type, ID, name and supported text up to 128 KiB. Select a result to inspect its source.


Fonts & Rendering
Font names below are requests and fallback choices, not proof of which installed font your browser selected. Imported monochrome bitmap fonts are used at matching sizes/styles when enabled in Appearance. Unsupported glyphs and strikes use browser fonts. Measurements show browser samples separately from bitmap coverage; fixed field baselines retain the stack's line height.


Saved Color & Pictures
Saved HCbg/HCcd declarations are previewed without running AddColor or HyperTalk. This report lists omitted or unsupported content; it does not infer dynamic script colors. Bevels and curved control shapes are approximate.
